week.worked: The armband was right. You put it on B.Fernandes and he scored a hat-trick. Mbeumo got the fifth in the same game. That is the whole reason you carry two United midfielders.
week.didnt: You scored 106 and went nowhere, still fifth of eleven. Kerkez has one point in two and Tzolis was hooked at half-time at Villa Park, so two of your outfield picks are doing nothing while the room banks the same captain you had.

big.call: Captain: B.Fernandes at Everton, or Haaland at home
big.why: You have had the armband on B.Fernandes and he goes to a ground that will spend the afternoon shouting at its own owners. Haaland is at home to Coventry, who have lost both and not scored, and he is City's only striker.

big.call: Kerkez: the seat is fine, the clean sheet is not
big.why: Liverpool signed no left-back and Iraola knows him from Bournemouth, so he keeps the shirt. They have also conceded twice in both games and bought nobody at the back. You are paying £5.5m for clean sheets that have not come.

watchlist.name: Palmer
watchlist.note: Your club's best player, and you still do not own him. 20 points in two, the penalties, and the price has moved twice since the brain first said so.

watchlist.name: Ødegaard
watchlist.note: You own Calafiori and Tzolis at the Emirates. The £6.6m midfielder outscoring both of them is the one you skipped.

week.worked: You played the Bench Boost in an ordinary week and all 15 of your players started. 151 points, and you lead the five by 29.
week.didnt: Nothing went wrong, so take the cost instead: the chip is spent and the other four still hold theirs. Your lead was bought once and it has to be defended without it.

big.call: Captain with the room, not against it
big.why: You lead by 29 with no chip left. The other four will nearly all put the armband on B.Fernandes or Haaland. If you match them, your lead can only shrink. A differential captain is the only thing that can grow it instead.

big.call: £8.0m of Coventry defenders you cannot start
big.why: van Ewijk and Thomas are both on your bench and Coventry go to the Etihad, the hardest fixture on the ticker at 5. The Bench Boost that made those two slots worth owning has already been spent.

watchlist.name: Hall
watchlist.note: 14 points at £5.1m, Burn out until mid-September, and Newcastle have the kindest six-game run in the game. You own nobody there.

week.worked: Gvardiol is yours alone in this room and he has 14 points. City now say O'Reilly is moving into midfield, so the left-back shirt you bought is the one he keeps.
week.didnt: Twelve points on your bench, second week running. Calvert-Lewin scored the Leeds equaliser while sitting on it, and Ndiaye is a Manchester City player now.

big.call: Ndiaye plays for Man City. Replace him
big.why: You bought Everton's main creator and he is now squad depth at the Etihad, behind Cherki and Foden at ten and Semenyo at nine. City have also just added Enzo Fernández. That is £6.0m of your eleven doing nothing.
He has started and scored in back-to-back weeks and you have benched him for both. Leeds go to Brighton. This one costs no transfer, only the order you write your team in.

watchlist.name: Dewsbury-Hall
watchlist.note: Everton sold Ndiaye, Beto and Patterson in a week and then lost Balogun. He is the creator left standing, at £6.5m, with United at home.

watchlist.name: Elanga
watchlist.note: 17 points at £6.1m in front of the best fixture run on the ticker. A straight swap for the man who left Everton.

week.worked: De Cuyper has 17 points at £4.7m and you are the only gaffer in the room who owns him. That call was yours and it is the best cheap defender any of the five bought.
week.didnt: 61 points and last of eleven. You were the one gaffer without B.Fernandes on the day he scored three, Tzolis was taken off at half-time, and Aït-Nouri has still not played a minute of football this season.

big.call: One transfer, two slots that do not play
big.why: Aït-Nouri has not played a minute this season and City call him third choice. Mosquera missed Arsenal's Thursday training and is doubtful for Chelsea. With £0.9m banked, you can fix one of them before 11pm.

big.call: Captain: Haaland at home, or João Pedro at the Emirates
big.why: You had the armband on João Pedro and Chelsea now go to Arsenal, the hardest fixture on the ticker at 5. Haaland is at home to Coventry, who have lost both and scored nothing. You are last of eleven and cannot afford another risky pick.

watchlist.name: Hall
watchlist.note: If the Aït-Nouri slot goes, this is what £5.1m buys: a defender who plays, with the kindest run in the game in front of him.

watchlist.name: Konsa
watchlist.note: The £4.4m insurance on your own Arsenal defender. Saliba is out for months and Mosquera missed Thursday's session.

week.worked: 107 points without spending a chip, and you are second. That is the same week Mr CR7 had and it took a Bench Boost to beat it.
week.didnt: 16 points on your bench, the most in the room. Groß scored at Stamford Bridge while sitting on it, Konsa came on as a substitute rather than starting, and Ndiaye now plays for Manchester City.

big.call: Your £6.0m Everton midfielder plays for Man City
big.why: Ndiaye left for £65m on deadline day. He keeps the price and loses the job. City call him squad depth behind Cherki, Foden and Semenyo. You have £0.5m in the bank to fix it with.

big.call: Konsa off your bench, not out of your squad
big.why: Saliba is out for months, Timber is only back on grass, and Mosquera missed Arsenal's open training on Thursday. At £4.4m your fourteenth man may start against Chelsea, and moving him up costs you nothing.

watchlist.name: White
watchlist.note: 18 points at £5.5m in the only defence yet to concede a league goal. You own the club and none of the players scoring for it.

watchlist.name: Gakpo
watchlist.note: City bid £80m and Liverpool said no, so he stays. Iraola then said he is happy with all four of his wingers, and one of the other three cost £123m.

watchlist.name: Palmer
watchlist.note: 20 points in two, the penalties, and a Chelsea side that sold Enzo Fernández and never replaced him. Nobody in the room owns him.

watchlist.name: Ødegaard
watchlist.note: Four of the five own an Arsenal defender and none owns the Arsenal player outscoring them, at £6.6m, with Chelsea at the Emirates.

watchlist.name: Cherki
watchlist.note: Still the most points of any midfielder in the game. Also sharing the number ten with Foden at a club that has just spent another £125m on a midfielder.

watchlist.name: Elanga
watchlist.note: Newcastle have the kindest six games on the ticker and he has 17 points at £6.1m. Not one of the five owns a Newcastle player.

watchlist.name: Hall
watchlist.note: The cheapest attacking defender at a settled club, and Burn is not back until mid-September. Same fixture run, £1.0m cheaper than the midfielder above.

watchlist.name: Ajayi
watchlist.note: 20 points at the cheapest defender price in the game, unflagged for Villa at home, and Hull's head coach says the six new arrivals have to earn shirts.

watchlist.name: Konsa
watchlist.note: £55m of centre-back at £4.4m, signed because Saliba and Timber are hurt, with the man ahead of him missing Thursday's training.

verdicts.name: B.Fernandes
verdicts.why: A hat-trick at Old Trafford, penalties, and four of the five had the armband on him.
verdicts.trigger: Two quiet weeks with United losing. At £12.0m the price only works while he is the whole team.

verdicts.name: Mbeumo
verdicts.why: Got the fifth against Ipswich and held his flank all afternoon.
verdicts.trigger: Rashford keeping the left and the returns concentrating there. Two blanks and £8.0m is the wrong United winger.

verdicts.name: Shaw
verdicts.why: United signed no left-back, so the shirt is his until January. Mazraoui came on for him against Ipswich and the club accept he cannot play 60 games at 31.
verdicts.trigger: Mazraoui starting a league game at left-back. That is the difference between a cheap defender who never misses and a rotation slot.

verdicts.name: Maguire
verdicts.why: Scored off a deflection and was the steady one in a defence that could have folded.
verdicts.trigger: Losing his place when United's other centre-backs are fit. The goal is a bonus, the seat is the asset.

verdicts.name: Lammens
verdicts.why: Kept United in the Ipswich game with first-half saves and was named the calm one in a panicked defence.
verdicts.trigger: Two more weeks conceding twice. You are paying £5.0m for a goalkeeper who saves shots but never keeps a clean sheet.

verdicts.name: Palmer
verdicts.why: 20 points in two games, the penalties, and Chelsea sold Enzo Fernández without signing a replacement.
verdicts.trigger: Two games spent wide rather than at ten, or the calf flag returning.

verdicts.name: João Pedro
verdicts.why: The reference point in Chelsea's attack, owned by all five, and Arsenal away is the hardest fixture on the ticker.
verdicts.trigger: Two Chelsea games without a shot in the box. At that ownership he becomes the risk rather than the floor.

verdicts.name: Rogers
verdicts.why: Three starts from three since the £117m move, and Arsenal wanted him at £80m before Chelsea paid more.
verdicts.trigger: A week wide right or on the bench. The Camara deal collapsing makes that less likely, not more.

verdicts.name: Martinez
verdicts.why: Chelsea have gone 18 games without a clean sheet, have conceded five in two, and go to the Emirates.
verdicts.trigger: One clean sheet. Until it comes he is a goalkeeper bought for save points at a club that concedes.

verdicts.name: Caicedo
verdicts.why: He has now missed three games and Chelsea expect him back around 12 September, which is Hull at home rather than Arsenal away.
verdicts.trigger: A league start. Chelsea never replaced him and the shirt is waiting, but not this week.

verdicts.name: Calafiori
verdicts.why: 20 points at £5.7m, the assist for Saka's winner at Villa Park, and a clean sheet with it. Four of the five own him.
verdicts.trigger: The knee trouble that follows him around, or Arsenal's European calendar producing real rotation.

verdicts.name: Saka
verdicts.why: The only goal at Villa Park, penalties at £9.5m, and Arsenal have now sold all three of the wide forwards who were competing with him.
verdicts.trigger: The recurring hamstring, or Arsenal finally buying a forward in January and the returns moving centrally.

verdicts.name: Havertz
verdicts.why: Martinelli's £60m move to Al-Hilal is now done, after Trossard and Jesus went the same way. He and Gyökeres are the entire senior forward line with Chelsea visiting.
verdicts.trigger: Gyökeres taking the shirt outright. Two games on the bench and £7.5m is a sack.

verdicts.name: Gyökeres
verdicts.why: Zero points in two at £7.3m, but he scored 21 in his first season and Arsenal are down to two senior forwards.
verdicts.trigger: A start and a goal in the next two. A £7.3m striker who has not scored by GW5 is not a striker.

verdicts.name: Ødegaard
verdicts.why: 14 points at £6.6m and a fortnight of nobody in the room owning him. That stopped being an oversight last week.
verdicts.trigger: A repeat of last season's injury record, or the returns concentrating in Saka alone.

verdicts.name: White
verdicts.why: 18 points at £5.5m in the only defence yet to concede a league goal, and two of the players who could take his place spent Thursday out of training.
verdicts.trigger: Timber getting past grass work and Saliba returning, which is not this side of the international break.

verdicts.name: Mosquera
verdicts.why: Thursday's trigger was a flag or Konsa named ahead of him. No flag has appeared, but he was missing from Arsenal's open training session on Thursday and is reported doubtful for Chelsea.
verdicts.trigger: Friday's session. He trains and starts, or The Special One is carrying a defender who does not play in the biggest fixture of the week.

verdicts.name: Konsa
verdicts.why: Saliba is out for months and Timber is only back on grass, and the man in front of him missed Thursday's training. At £4.4m that is a starting centre-back priced as a bench slot.
verdicts.trigger: Chelsea's visit. He starts and this goes to solid. Mosquera trains on Friday and plays, and £4.4m stays a bench place.

verdicts.name: Tzolis
verdicts.why: Reversing Monday's sack, which graded a £34m winger on 45 bad minutes. He impressed in the Community Shield win over City and on the opening day against Coventry, and Arsenal have just sold both of their other left-sided forwards.
verdicts.trigger: A second half-time substitution, or Eze starting ahead of him against Chelsea. Then it is a sack and it stays one.

verdicts.name: Eze
verdicts.why: He set up Saka's winner after coming on at half time, and Arsenal have sold three forwards and had two attackers miss Thursday's session. At £6.4m and 1.5% he is the cheap way in.
verdicts.trigger: A start against Chelsea. If Arteta gives him the shirt in that fixture the price is wrong by a long way.

verdicts.name: Haaland
verdicts.why: Owned by all five, at home to Coventry, and now City's only first-team striker after Marmoush went to Spurs and Mubama went on loan.
verdicts.trigger: A serious injury. City spent a record £458m and did not buy a back-up, so there is no version of this where he plays less.

verdicts.name: Gvardiol
verdicts.why: City are reported to be lining O'Reilly up at the base of midfield against Coventry, and Guéhi played there against Bournemouth. That leaves one senior left-back at the club.
verdicts.trigger: Doku back and City going wider with O'Reilly restored to defence. Nothing said this week points that way.

verdicts.name: Cherki
verdicts.why: Still the highest-scoring midfielder in the game, and still owned by none of the five. City now have two established players in almost every position and Maresca has a selection dilemma every week.
verdicts.trigger: Two starts in a row at number ten. He shares that shirt with Foden and has never reached ten Premier League goals in a season.

verdicts.name: Semenyo
verdicts.why: One assist all season at £8.5m. He is still the only City attacker to hit double figures in the league in the last two seasons, and the club see him as the cover at number nine.
verdicts.trigger: A goal against Coventry at home. If it does not come in that fixture, £8.5m is a sack.

verdicts.name: Ndiaye
verdicts.why: Settled by the transfer and confirmed by the club: City signed him for versatility and squad depth, behind Cherki and Foden at ten and Semenyo at nine.
verdicts.trigger: Settled. Two of the five own him and both should be spending the £6.0m elsewhere.

verdicts.name: Aït-Nouri
verdicts.why: City refused United's deadline-day loan and now say they are well stocked at left-back. Unused substitute in all three games.
verdicts.trigger: A start. Until then this is a squad place doing no work whatever.

verdicts.name: Gakpo
verdicts.why: Iraola said he was glad to keep him and called him valuable after City's £80m was rejected. He also said he is happy with all four wingers, and one of the other three cost £123m.
verdicts.trigger: Barcola starting on the left at Ipswich. 17 points at £7.1m are real. The shirt is the question and Friday night answers it.

verdicts.name: Szoboszlai
verdicts.why: Liverpool sold Jones and signed nobody in central midfield, so the minutes are there. They also failed to sign a right-back and name him as cover, which is where the penalties stop.
verdicts.trigger: One game at right-back. Three of the five own him at £7.0m and a full-back does not take spot kicks.

verdicts.name: Kerkez
verdicts.why: Monday's sack was about who starts, and that was never the problem. Liverpool signed no left-back and Iraola worked with him at Bournemouth. The problem is that Liverpool have conceded twice in both league games.
verdicts.trigger: A clean sheet at Ipswich or against Fulham. Two soft fixtures in a row without one and £5.5m is a sack for the right reason.

verdicts.name: Barry
verdicts.why: Balogun never arrived, Beto is sold, and Everton go into United at home with one senior striker at £5.5m.
verdicts.trigger: Everton signing a free agent forward, or two blanks against United and Spurs.

verdicts.name: Dewsbury-Hall
verdicts.why: 13 points at £6.5m, and Everton have sold Ndiaye, Iroegbunam and Patterson and lost Balogun inside four days.
verdicts.trigger: Grealish taking the creative burden instead. That is one team sheet away and worth watching before it costs anything.

verdicts.name: Tarkowski
verdicts.why: Everton's captain on set pieces, 18 points, and United visiting a ground that will spend the afternoon shouting at its own directors' box.
verdicts.trigger: Two games without a header or a clean sheet. Then this is a set-piece bet rather than a defender.

verdicts.name: Elanga
verdicts.why: Opened the scoring at Spurs, 17 points at £6.1m, in front of the kindest six games on the ticker.
verdicts.trigger: Fernandez-Pardo taking his flank now the £51.4m is spent. That is the only thing that ends this.

verdicts.name: Wissa
verdicts.why: Scored at Spurs and the competition left. Woltemade has gone to Juventus on loan, so the shirt is his at £6.1m.
verdicts.trigger: Fernandez-Pardo being played centrally, or two blanks in the easiest run in the league.

verdicts.name: Hall
verdicts.why: 14 points at £5.1m in a side with the softest six games on the ticker, and United wanted him all summer before deciding the fee was too big.
verdicts.trigger: Burn returning around 14 September and the left side going back. Until then this is the cheapest attacking defender at a settled club.

verdicts.name: Kinsky
verdicts.why: Owned by three of the five at a club that is bottom, has not scored in two, and has just left its most experienced forward out of the squad entirely.
verdicts.trigger: Reassess at GW7 once the window is shut, players are settled, and fixtures are softer. Until then this is a bench goalkeeper.

verdicts.name: Verbruggen
verdicts.why: Leeds visit having lost Rodon for eight to ten weeks, with Gudmundsson also hurt and a full-back likely to fill in at centre-back.
verdicts.trigger: A clean sheet against Leeds. Three of the five own him and a £4.5m goalkeeper is bought for exactly this fixture.

verdicts.name: De Cuyper
verdicts.why: 17 points at £4.7m, but the last of them came from an advanced role he was not bought for.
verdicts.trigger: A return to left-back and a clean sheet. £4.7m for a makeshift winger is the wrong position at the wrong price.

verdicts.name: Groß
verdicts.why: Crossed for one and headed in another at Stamford Bridge, on penalties at £5.5m. All three owners had him on the bench.
verdicts.trigger: A start in the room's elevens, or two weeks without a return. At 33 the minutes are the question.

verdicts.name: Calvert-Lewin
verdicts.why: Scored again, started again, and two of his four owners in this room still have him on a bench.
verdicts.trigger: Losing the penalties, or Leeds changing the shape around him.

verdicts.name: Schade
verdicts.why: Scored at Elland Road at £6.0m, and he is the Brentford attacker whose place has not been bought over.
verdicts.trigger: Thiago rediscovering the shirt, or two blanks in a side that has drawn twice.

verdicts.name: M.Sangaré
verdicts.why: 18 points at £5.7m and 14.2% ownership, which is the best value in the midfield and was declined here on debut.
verdicts.trigger: Two blanks. A midfielder scoring at this price is the cheapest way to fill an eleven and D13 says stop declining them.

verdicts.name: Ajayi
verdicts.why: Unflagged for Villa at home, and Hull's head coach has made it clear the deadline-day arrivals have to earn shirts rather than inherit them.
verdicts.trigger: Norton-Cuffy starting at right-back. Buy the man himself. The six arrivals are still a squad competing for places.

verdicts.name: Tzolakis
verdicts.why: 20 points from two clean sheets at £4.6m, and 19 summer signings have not touched the goalkeeper.
verdicts.trigger: Hull conceding in both of the next two. Villa at home is the first honest test of the shape.

verdicts.name: Hume
verdicts.why: Sunderland kept their first clean sheet at £4.5m, then spent £30m on Fofana and took Danso on loan.
verdicts.trigger: Danso or Fofana starting in the back four. A £4.5m defender survives one signing, rarely two.

verdicts.name: E.Le Fée
verdicts.why: Sunderland won without him producing anything, and the case at £5.9m was always that the side plays through him.
verdicts.trigger: A return in the next two, or the money goes to a midfielder who takes shots.

verdicts.name: Cash
verdicts.why: Villa have lost both, spent £76m on Mbaye and Harwood-Bellis, and gave Wan-Bissaka his debut at right-back on 78 minutes.
verdicts.trigger: Two clean sheets in three with him playing all of them. Nothing shorter.

verdicts.name: Wilson
verdicts.why: Four points in two at £6.4m, and Leeds go to Brighton with Calvert-Lewin taking the goals and the penalties.
verdicts.trigger: A return at Brighton. A £6.4m midfielder who is neither the scorer nor the taker is the wrong Leeds player.

verdicts.name: Bruno G.
verdicts.why: The £75m midfielder was the second absentee from Thursday's open training, with a groin problem that goes back to the Community Shield. He has one Arsenal appearance.
verdicts.trigger: A start against Chelsea. Until then £6.8m buys a player nobody has seen finish a week fit.

verdicts.name: Richarlison
verdicts.why: Spurs left him out of their Premier League squad entirely. He cannot be selected before January whatever happens on the pitch.
verdicts.trigger: Settled. A player outside the registered squad is not a bench option, he is an empty slot.

verdicts.name: Guéhi
verdicts.why: 18.8% of the game owns a £6.0m City defender, and Maresca played him in holding midfield against Bournemouth with Rodri and Nico González both gone.
verdicts.trigger: Two league starts in midfield. A defender who never stands in the back four cannot keep a clean sheet, whatever the shirt says.

verdicts.name: Barcola
verdicts.why: £123m, trained all week, and available at Ipswich on Friday. Iraola says he is happy with the four wingers he has, which is four players for two flanks.
verdicts.trigger: Two starts on the left. At £8.0m he needs the shirt, not the fee, and the first team sheet answers it.

signals.text: Arsenal held an open training session on Thursday and both Cristhian Mosquera and Bruno Guimarães were absent from it. Saliba is out for months after aggravating a back injury at the World Cup and Timber has only just returned to grass work.
signals.action: the champions' back four is not settled with Chelsea visiting. White and Konsa are the two most likely to start it, and Mosquera is the one to check at 10pm

signals.text: City spent more than £300m on midfielders and still look light at No 6. Maresca used Marc Guéhi in the holding role against Bournemouth, Ayyoub Bouaddi is 18 and being eased in, and "O'Reilly may line up at the base of midfield for Coventry's visit".
signals.action: City's two mid-priced defenders are being used as midfielders. If you want the City clean sheet against Coventry, Gvardiol is the only one of them standing in the back four

signals.text: Iraola says he is "very happy" with all four signings and defended not buying a right-back or a central midfielder: "There were other options that we decided not to take." He is "happy with the four wingers we have", and Barcola is available at Ipswich.
signals.action: four wingers for two flanks, and no cover at right-back. Liverpool's attackers are a rotation this week, and their defenders have conceded twice in both games

signals.text: Caicedo has missed three matches and is expected back around 12 September, Henderson is still recovering from a World Cup wrist injury, and Palestra was absent from Thursday's training. Chelsea let 39 players leave this summer.
signals.action: Chelsea travel to the Emirates with a thin midfield and five goals conceded in two games. Their defenders and goalkeeper are not clean-sheet buys this week

signals.text: 19 signings since promotion, seven of them in the final week. "Jakirovic needs to decide whether to incorporate these potential upgrades into his starting XI as soon as possible or make them earn the shirts... he values loyalty and no one will walk into the side he has built."
signals.action: Monday's read was wrong. The back four that kept two clean sheets is more likely to start than not, so the £4.0m Hull defenders are buyable again. Buy one of them rather than the whole back four.

signals.text: Farke: "Bad news, serious hamstring injury. He will be out for eight to 10 weeks." Rodon has started every game. Gudmundsson is also out with a hamstring, Bard only signed on deadline day, and Farke says "we may need James Justin at centre-back".
signals.action: Leeds go to Brighton with an improvised centre-back pairing. That is a reason to start Verbruggen and a reason not to buy a Leeds defender

signals.text: Everton go into United at home with one senior striker after the Balogun collapse. The crowd is aimed at the owners rather than the visitors. The 1878s have withdrawn the flag displays and there are calls for a "not a pound in the ground" campaign.
signals.action: the goals and the creation are concentrated in two players at £5.5m and £6.5m. Everton's clean sheet is not the bet. Their front two are.

signals.text: Bottom of the table with no goals in two games having spent more than £300m, and now leaving Richarlison out of the Premier League squad altogether. Forest are expected to start Liam Delap against them.
signals.action: three of the five own Kinsky at £4.5m as a clean-sheet bet on a side that has kept none and scored none. Forest away is not the week it starts

signals.text: Missing from Arsenal's open training session on Thursday, two days after coming off injured at Villa Park with Konsa replacing him. Arteta had described the substitution as a precaution. No flag has appeared in the player file.
signals.action: he is unflagged, so he stays in an eleven by default. Check the Friday session before the 11pm deadline. A defender who does not start scores you zero points

signals.text: The second absentee from Thursday's open training, with a groin problem that dates back to the Community Shield. The £75m signing has made one Arsenal appearance, against Villa.
signals.action: nobody in the room owns him and nobody should buy him this week. A £6.8m midfielder who cannot get through a training week is not a pick

signals.text: Signed for £55m "because of the injuries to William Saliba and Jurrien Timber". Saliba is out for months, Timber is back on grass only, and Mosquera missed Thursday's session.
signals.action: Le Professeur has him on the bench at £4.4m. Move him into the eleven before the deadline rather than transferring anyone out

signals.text: Martinelli's £60m move to Al-Hilal is confirmed, following Trossard to Beşiktaş and Jesus to Barcelona. Arsenal chased Vinícius Jr, Rogers, Barcola and Álvarez and signed none of them.
signals.action: he and Gyökeres are the whole senior forward line with Chelsea at the Emirates. One of the two starts every week now

signals.text: "Nico O'Reilly may line up at the base of midfield for Coventry's visit", and Guéhi was used in the holding role against Bournemouth. City called Aït-Nouri third choice behind Gvardiol and O'Reilly.
signals.action: the left-back shirt is his and the two men who could take it are being played in midfield. Coventry have not scored a league goal

signals.text: "Maresca deployed Marc Guéhi in a holding midfield role against Bournemouth" with Rodri and Nico González both gone and Bouaddi only 18.
signals.action: 18.8% of the game owns him as a £6.0m defender. A defender playing No 6 keeps the price and loses the clean sheet

signals.text: "Haaland is now City's only first-team striker" after Marmoush went to Spurs and Mubama went on loan. Maresca is "not fazed", with Semenyo the deputy centre-forward.
signals.action: no back-up means no rest weeks, and Coventry at home. All five own him and none of them should be hunting for a reason not to captain him

signals.text: "The last midfield spot, the number 10 position, has been shared between Foden and Cherki." Of City's attacking options only Semenyo has reached double figures in the league in the last two seasons.
signals.action: the highest-scoring midfielder in the game, in a straight rotation, at a club that has just added Enzo Fernández and Ndiaye. Wait for the team sheet

signals.text: "Antoine Semenyo is an able deputy centre-forward if Erling Haaland is unavailable." He is also the only City attacker to reach double figures in the league in the last two seasons.
signals.action: one assist at £8.5m, and Coventry at home is the fixture the trigger was written for. Hold rather than sell before it

signals.text: City describe the £65m signing as someone who "adds greater versatility and squad depth", behind Cherki and Foden at ten and Semenyo at nine. He has never reached double figures in a Premier League season.
signals.action: two of the five still own him at £6.0m on an Everton price tag. This is the transfer to make before 11pm

signals.text: "Effectively that is Shaw as first-choice left-back, with Noussair Mazraoui as back-up", and "it is widely accepted 31-year-old Shaw will not be able to play repeatedly in a new campaign that could stretch beyond 60 games."
signals.action: his place in the squad is safe until January, but he does not always play 90 minutes. Treat him as a cheap defender who might get rotated

signals.text: "Bradley Barcola has trained with his Liverpool team-mates this week" and "will be available for selection" at Ipswich on Friday. He cost £123m.
signals.action: he is £8.0m and 1.1% owned with no minutes yet. Watch which flank he starts on before paying for him

signals.text: Iraola was "glad to keep Cody Gakpo because he is a valuable player" after City's £80m bid was rejected, and separately said he is "happy with the four wingers we have".
signals.action: he stays, but so do three other wingers including a £123m one. 17 points at £7.1m, and Friday night tells you whether the shirt is still his

signals.text: Liverpool let Curtis Jones go to Inter and signed no replacement, leaving Iraola "four senior central midfielders". They also failed to sign a right-back, where "Araujo can also play, and so can Dominik Szoboszlai, if needed".
signals.action: the central minutes are safer than they were a week ago and the right-back risk has not gone. Three of the five hold him at £7.0m for penalties

signals.text: "Milos Kerkez has had an underwhelming start but the hope is that he can peak under Iraola, whom he worked with at Bournemouth." Liverpool signed no left-back and have conceded twice in both games.
signals.action: the shirt is not the problem, the clean sheets are. Judge him on Ipswich away and Fulham at home

signals.text: He lasted 14 minutes against Brighton before limping off and has now missed three matches. Chelsea expect him back around 12 September, for the Hull game at home rather than the Arsenal game away.
signals.action: listed as a 75% doubt in the player file, which overstates it for this week. Not a buy before the Emirates

signals.text: Balogun "pulled out of the Everton move over the handling of his medical", four days after Everton sold Beto and accepted Forest's £35m for Armstrong. Sutton: "at least they still have him to lead their line."
signals.action: the trigger was a striker arriving to take his shirt and nobody did. £5.5m, 4.6% owned, United at home

signals.text: "Richarlison is left out of Tottenham's Premier League squad as he does not figure in the club's plans this season." He cannot be registered again until January.
signals.action: sell or ignore. A player outside the squad list is not a cheap bench forward, he is an empty shirt at £5.9m

signals.text: Hull made 19 signings. Jakirovic says "no one has let down the head coach or the fans over 180 minutes, so it would be harsh to drop anyone" and that he "values loyalty and will want to challenge the mentality of the new arrivals".
signals.action: the cheapest defender in the game with 20 points, unflagged for Villa at home, and the six new arrivals are not walking into the side. Buy him

doctrine.text: Protecting your rank has a real cost. Price the drift on every call.
New-manager minutes are unknowable until three XIs.
Champions' template players are the default owns. Passing on them needs a priced case.
Opening weekend prices nothing. A promoted side beating a giant is one result until the same shape holds twice. Sell on a pattern, never on a scoreline.
A cheap-defender haul only tells you about one match. Before buying points that already happened, check the player is still fit and still first choice.

Grade a chip against its own median week. Then check the table before saying it did not matter. Six points from a Bench Boost is a chip spent rather than used. It is also the six points between first of the five and second.

Buy the line-up. Ignore the scoreboard. Three of the weekend's best mid-price returns came from players who started on a bench or out of position. Two of the room's bench slots are held by players who have not been in a matchday eleven.

A player the whole room passed on is a bigger exposure than a player the whole room owns. All five owned Haaland and João Pedro. None owned Palmer, who outscored both. Check the consensus blind spot before checking the consensus pick.

An open window changes who plays before it changes who you should buy. Buy after the window shuts. It paid on 1 September. Two of the five went to bed owning an Everton midfielder and woke up owning a Manchester City substitute, and nobody who waited lost anything by waiting.

A cup tie tells you about the team sheet more than the result. The goals are worth nothing and the selection is worth everything. That is why a 35-year-old's header, a flagged striker's replacement and a vice-captain's absence were the three things worth reading on Thursday night.

Write triggers a transfer can settle, not only ones that need 90 minutes. Deadline day settled six calls here without a ball being kicked. They were the Liverpool winger, the Arsenal forward, the United left-back, the Everton striker, the Everton midfielder and the City left-back. A trigger only a scoreline can fire sits open through the weeks that decide the player.

A room that agrees has no protection against being wrong together. Not one of the five captained Haaland this week. The three who did in GW1 all moved off him. He scored twice at Palace before any of their captains had kicked a ball. Check what the room has agreed on, not only what it argues about.

Grade a rule by what it cost. Do not grade it by how sensible it sounded. D5 declined the £4.0m Hull defenders after one haul because they were flagged and it was one match. Two weeks on Hull have six points, two clean sheets, and the two best-scoring £4.0m defenders in the game. A rule that only ever says no stops being useful.

A Bench Boost wants 15 players who start. It does not need a double gameweek. The page called Sir Fergie's chip premature on Saturday. By Sunday night every one of his 15 had played, and it had won him the week and the lead. Grade a chip by the team sheet it lands on. The calendar does not matter.

A player sold inside the league has not gone, he has just moved clubs. The price on his card does not move for a week either. Ndiaye is worth £6.0m in two of these squads this morning and is fourth in the queue at his new club. Read the new shirt, forget the old fee.

Do not grade a player on 45 minutes. Three sacks were reversed on Wednesday. They were a winger hooked at half-time, a defender who came on as a substitute, and a left-back who was never actually dropped. It happened again on Thursday. The Hull back four sacked on Monday for six deadline-day arrivals turns out to be the back four the head coach intends to keep. Wait for the second data point when the first one is a substitution.

The injury flag moves last, after the news is already out. Arsenal's centre-back missed Thursday's open training with Chelsea to come and carries no flag in the player file. The £75m midfielder beside him missed it too. A squad that is picked on Friday afternoon is reported on Thursday night and flagged on Saturday morning. Read the training ground first, then the file.

roast.text: Sir Fergie played his Bench Boost in an ordinary week, all 15 of his players started, and it won him the week and the lead. He is now the only man in the room whose best idea is behind him.

plan.outlook: Deadline day, the window is shut, and for the first time this season the team sheets are the story rather than the transfers. Arsenal held an open training session on Thursday and two of their players were missing from it, which makes the £4.4m defender on Le Professeur's bench more interesting than anything either of them could buy. City are lining a £6.5m defender up in midfield and played a £6.0m one there last week, which leaves Gvardiol as the only City defender actually defending. Hull's head coach says his 19 signings have to earn shirts, so the cheap back four the brain cooled on Monday is buyable again. Sir Fergie leads by 29 with his chip gone. Mr CR7 and Le Professeur each have £6.0m sitting in a Manchester City squad player. The Special One has one transfer and two men who may not play.

chips.note: First-half chips die at the GW19 deadline (2 Jan). Two have been played and neither waited for a double gameweek: Le Professeur's returned six points in GW1, Sir Fergie's returned the best week anyone has had and the lead. The difference was that all 15 of Sir Fergie's players started. The window is shut and the squads stop moving under the chip now, so GW6–8 is the first honest Wildcard, with three settled line-ups behind it.

log.call: Day-0 squad: Haaland (C) vs BOU; bets on Palmer, Kerkez, Hume; passed on Bruno Fernandes at £12.0m with Mbeumo/Shaw/Lammens carrying the Man Utd run.

Held again with GW1 unfinished: no transfer, the free one banked to Friday, all three United men kept into Ipswich at home. Haaland (C) at Selhurst Park, B.Fernandes vice, 3-4-3 unchanged. Declined the Hull £4.0m defenders after their haul.

No move with Gameweek 1 one fixture from finished. Declined all three of the weekend's obvious buys — the Hull £4.0m defenders (all flagged at 75%), Sangaré's fourteen on debut, and Cherki's eight off the bench — on the grounds that a doubt or a substitute is not a seat. Graded Le Professeur's Gameweek 1 Bench Boost as spent rather than used at six points, while conceding he leads the five without it.

Settled Gameweek 1 at fifty points and fifth of eleven. Upgraded Palmer to nailed after thirteen on the opening night and named him, with Ødegaard, as the room's shape rather than its luck — neither is owned by any of the five. Sacked Palestra and Aït-Nouri as slots rather than players after both missed their clubs' matchday elevens, and sacked Cash and Watkins on Villa's week rather than on Villa's fixture. Recommended no transfer before Friday: every obvious buy is either one game old, flagged, or in the middle of a transfer.

No transfer recommended for the third run running, two days before the deadline and six before the window shuts — on the explicit grounds that an open window is a team-sheet risk rather than a shopping opportunity (D9). Downgraded Shaw on the reporting that United expect another left-back before Tuesday. Flipped the Gakpo case: the risk is no longer that Liverpool sell him but that they buy over him, with two bids rejected for one winger and two more targets live. Sacked Villa's goalkeeper as a slot, and Forest's incumbent striker on a £50m arrival. Corrected two errors of our own from Monday: The Special One's dead men were on his bench, not in his eleven, and Le Professeur's six-point Bench Boost is not a footnote to his lead, it is the whole of it.

Deadline eve, and no transfer recommended for the fifth run running — Friday’s deadline falls four days before the window shuts, so nothing bought now is bought with the team sheet known. Upgraded Woltemade on Osula’s knock and a cup start, and opened Barry at £5.5m on a hat-trick graded as a team sheet rather than a scoreline. Held Palestra at sack after Alonso said Chelsea "need to check a little bit more" ahead of a second missed fixture, and added the goalkeeper question alongside it. Cooled De Cuyper on Brighton’s injury list rather than on his seventeen points, and warned on Ajer as Brentford bought a fifth player and sold a centre-back. Sacked Baleba, Osula and Grealish as slots rather than players. Minted D10: a cup tie is a team sheet, not a fixture.

Deadline day. No transfer recommended for the sixth run running, on the grounds that the deadline falls four days before the window shuts and every squad in the room already has fifteen fit players. Settled two calls by transfer rather than by result: sacked Sánchez outright once Chelsea agreed £7.5m for Martinez, the exact trigger written on Monday, and killed the Gakpo case once Liverpool agreed £120m for Barcola — the trigger there was the window shutting with nobody arriving, and somebody arrived. Opened Martinez at £5.0m as a Tuesday buy rather than a Friday one, with Suzuki alongside him. Upgraded Woltemade to solid as Osula went from a 50% knock to no return date, and Konsa on the reporting that he starts at Villa Park. Downgraded Penders to sack behind the new goalkeeper. Cooled Guéhi on the grounds that his ten points came from central midfield, where a defender keeps no clean sheets. Opened Estêvão, James, Acheampong, Trafford, Tarkowski and Tonali. Minted D11: write triggers a transfer can settle, not only ones that need ninety minutes.

Saturday of a gameweek one fixture old. Upgraded Cherki to nailed on the start his trigger asked for, plus two goals at Selhurst Park, and recorded that not one of the five captained Haaland before he scored twice. Moved Guéhi back towards a buy once Maresca dropped the midfield experiment and played him at centre-back. Settled Watkins on the £50m Al-Hilal sale and Martinez on Villa confirming the Chelsea deal. Opened Foden, O'Reilly, Diouf, Delap and Muñoz. Recommended no transfer again, on the grounds that the window shuts on Tuesday and the GW3 deadline is the Friday after it — the first week of the season in which waiting costs nothing. Minted D12 on the armband.

Saturday's five fixtures settled four open triggers and opened a hole. Upgraded Tarkowski to solid on the late goal at Bournemouth, exactly the trigger written on Thursday. Sacked Tonali, whose trigger was ninety minutes against Newcastle and who was substituted in a 2-0 defeat, and sacked Gravenberch, who was left out of the pivot rather than keeping a clean sheet in it. Moved Igor Jesus back to watch after he started at Anfield ahead of the £45m Delap, and cooled Delap for the same reason. Cooled Kerkez after he was taken off on 71 minutes, and cooled Woltemade after Wissa scored at Spurs and Napoli were reported to want him on loan. Settled Sánchez and Muñoz by transfer. Opened Isak, Gibbs-White, Elanga, Wissa, Scott and the three Hull picks. Minted D13 against the brain's own D5: the £4.0m Hull defenders it declined after one haul now have two clean sheets behind them and thirty-six points between them. Recommended no transfer until the window shuts on Tuesday.

Gameweek 2 settled everything except Villa v Arsenal. Marked the brain's own Bench Boost rule under review after Sir Fergie played one in a single gameweek and won the week and the lead with it — D14. Upgraded B.Fernandes on a hat-trick that fired his blank trigger the other way, and upgraded Maguire, Lammens, Schade, Calvert-Lewin, Wissa, Ajayi and Tzolakis. Sacked Lacroix on the exact trigger written on Thursday — a clean sheet against a depleted Brighton — after Chelsea conceded three and reached eighteen games without one. Sacked Caicedo, who came off in tears after eleven minutes, Kerkez a week early on the substitution rather than the missed start, Welbeck on an unused bench at 4-3, and Woltemade once Wissa started and scored. Cooled Ndiaye with Spurs in advanced talks, Semenyo on one assist at £8.5m, De Cuyper on an advanced role that is not the position he was bought for, and Havertz on Arsenal chasing Álvarez. Opened Rashford, Neto and Groß. Recommended no transfer until the window shuts on Tuesday, with the deadline three days behind it.

First run with the window shut. Recommended the room's first transfers of the season. Ndiaye out for Mr CR7 and Le Professeur after his £65m move to Manchester City, and Aït-Nouri out for The Special One on City calling him third-choice left-back. Reversed three sacks that deadline day settled the other way. Gakpo stays after Liverpool rejected £80m. Shaw keeps his place after United failed to sign a left-back. Barry becomes Everton's only striker after the Balogun deal collapsed. Sacked Tzolis on a 4/10 and a half-time substitution, and Konsa on coming off the bench rather than starting. Cooled Cherki, Foden and Semenyo on City signing two more attackers, and cooled the whole Hull back four on six deadline-day arrivals and the sale of a defender who had played all three games. Promoted D9 to doctrine on the evidence it just produced, retired D6 into D14, and minted D15 on players sold inside the league.

Deadline eve. Reversed three of Monday's own sacks after reading the window post-mortems. Tzolis was graded on 45 minutes, but impressed in the Community Shield and on the opening day. Konsa was signed because Saliba and Timber are injured, and the man ahead of him limped off. Kerkez stays because Liverpool signed no left-back and Iraola knows him from Bournemouth. Upgraded Gvardiol to nailed on City saying O'Reilly moves into midfield, which reverses last week's trigger. Downgraded Szoboszlai on Liverpool naming him as right-back cover, and Gakpo on Barcola's likely debut at Ipswich. Upgraded Ajayi on the flag coming off. Recommended captaincy calls rather than transfers for three of the five, and minted D16. A verdict written on 45 minutes proves nothing.

Deadline day, window shut. Read the training ground rather than the player file. Mosquera and Bruno Guimarães both missed Arsenal's open session on Thursday. Downgraded Mosquera without a flag, moved Konsa and White up, and told Le Professeur to promote Konsa off his bench rather than spend a transfer. Reversed Monday's cooling of the Hull back four after Jakirovic said the six deadline-day arrivals must earn shirts, and put Ajayi back on the house list. Opened Barcola, Guéhi and Bruno G., and sacked Richarlison outright. He was left out of Spurs' registered Premier League squad. Upgraded Verbruggen on Rodon's eight-to-ten-week hamstring and Leeds improvising at centre-back. Repeated the Ndiaye transfer for the two owners and the Aït-Nouri sale for The Special One. Minted D17. The flag moves last, not first.
